# Vendored files

Browser libraries and fonts are copied here. There are no CDNs (strict CSP). When you change a file, update its row. CI fails if a file is unlisted, missing, or its SHA-256 differs.

The game's files (`fonts.css`, `fonts/`, `gsap.min.js`) live in `app/vendor/`; `python3 app/build.py` copies them here and never deletes this file or other vendored files. Change them in `app/vendor/`, rebuild, then update the row. The check also fails if a file in `app/vendor/` differs from its row.

The resume reader's libraries (`pdfjs/`, `mammoth/`) are used only by the adult app (`/work/`) and are loaded only after a person picks a file. They live only here, not in `app/vendor/`; the student build does not touch them. Each was taken unchanged from its npm package (registry.npmjs.org), at a version more than two weeks old on 29 Oct 2026. To update one, download the new package, copy the same files, and change the row.

The on-device skill reader's library (`transformers/`) is used only by the adult app (`/work/`) and is loaded only after a person agrees to the tier 2 reading (BUILD_PLAN T4.5; `app/adult/intake_embed.js` is the only file that imports it). `transformers.min.js` is the self-contained browser bundle of `@huggingface/transformers` 4.3.2 (Apache-2.0; published on npm 2026-10-27, see docs/adult/deviations.md D43 on its age). It includes onnxruntime-web 1.31.0-dev.20260914-8d85527a0, the version that release pins. The two `ort-wasm-simd-threaded` files are that onnxruntime-web package's single-thread WebAssembly runtime (MIT), the plain build and not the 26.9 MB `.asyncify` build, which is over the 25 MiB file limit of Cloudflare Pages. The app points the library at these files and turns off every remote path (`env.allowRemoteModels = false`), so no request leaves this site. The model files are not here: they are fetched at build time, pinned and hash-checked (`app/adult/tools/tier2_model.json`), and served from `/work/models/`. To update: download the new npm packages, copy the same files, change the rows, and re-run the tier 2 tests.

What to know about this library before you accept it (S5 review S8, docs/adult/deviations.md D43; checked 2026-11-10 against the npm packages):
- **The runtime is a development (nightly) build, not a release.** The version string is `1.31.0-dev.20260914-8d85527a0`, built on 2026-09-14. Every release of `@huggingface/transformers` that we looked at pins a development build of `onnxruntime-web` (4.2.0 pins `1.26.0-dev.20260416-b7804b056c`; 4.3.0, 4.3.1 and 4.3.2 all pin `1.31.0-dev.20260914-8d85527a0`). The model vectors in `data/graph/` were made with the stable `onnxruntime-node` 1.30.0 (the library's Node dependency), so the browser and the vector tool do not run the same build; the tests check that the browser and Node give the same numbers on the fixtures (D47).
- **Age.** 4.3.2 was published on npm at 2026-10-27 18:15 UTC and vendored on 2026-11-10: 14 days, so it met the two-week habit only on the day. The rule is a habit, not a CI check.
- **4.3.1** (published 2026-10-06, 35 days old on 2026-11-10) pins the same `onnxruntime-web` development build as 4.3.2, so taking 4.3.1 does not make the runtime stable. Its `dist/transformers.min.js` is 586,230 bytes (this one is 587,917). Its plain (non-asyncify) WebAssembly runtime is the same 14,264,838-byte file, under the 25 MiB (26,214,400 bytes) limit of Cloudflare Pages; the asyncify build is over it in either version.
- A stable `onnxruntime-web` exists (1.31.1, published 2026-10-26; its plain `ort-wasm-simd-threaded.wasm` is 14,848,852 bytes, also under the limit). The library's self-contained bundle holds the JavaScript half of the runtime, so replacing only the two runtime files by hand would mix two builds. We did not try that and do not recommend it without a test of the real model in a browser.
- Decision for the owner: accept 4.3.2 with the nightly runtime (what is here), take 4.3.1 (no gain on this point), or wait for a library release that pins a stable runtime.
- Inlined packages: the bundle also contains `@huggingface/jinja` and `@huggingface/tokenizers` (their error messages are in it), and `onnxruntime-common` (part of onnxruntime-web). Their licence texts are the two `LICENSE-huggingface-*` files below; `onnxruntime-common` is in the onnxruntime repository, covered by `LICENSE-onnxruntime`.

Check by hand: `node .github/scripts/check_vendor_hashes.mjs`
